title: Contact size placement lowered mean variance by less than 1.1 percent in two selected mouse failure models
abstract: We tested whether contact size placement changes variance under a fixed spatial failure law in two selected mouse cortex maps. We kept each connection, all contact positions, and its full size distribution fixed. We compared observed size placement with random assignments to the same positions. A Poisson ball model used radius 10 micrometres and survival probability 0.9. Mean normalized variance was 1.081 percent below the exact assignment mean in 1,519 Allen V1DD connections and 0.825 percent below it in 1,472 MICrONS connections. Two-sided probabilities from 1,999 assignments were 0.001 and 0.004; correction for two maps gave 0.002 and 0.008. Mean differences remained negative across tested radii and cell-weighted summaries. Fewer than half of connections were below their own assignment mean at the primary settings. Independent scalar calculations checked all 2,991 connections. The failure law and linear size weights are assumptions. One mouse per map, incomplete arbors, branch effects and absent matched activity prevent a biological reliability claim. The package gives new code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps. External contact records are not bundled.

display.caption: Observed size placement gives small reductions in mean normalized variance against fixed-connection size assignments in two selected mouse maps. Ranges are conditional null ranges, not animal confidence intervals.
